name: S-Class Skald
body:
What are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced. The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—a summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

S-class skalds brave the world with shield and song, fighting alongside the warriors of their clan and keeping their spirits up while doing so. Their frenzied inspiration drives a battle in favor of their allies, and their leadership leads their party to victory more often than not.

Note: The s-class skald is an alternate, superior version of the skald class. They retain all of the standard skald progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select skald archetypes without specific adjustments.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8.

Parent Classes: Barbarian and bard.

Starting Wealth: 3d6 × 10 gp (average 105 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class skald’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (all) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (oratory, percussion, sing, string, wind) (Cha), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class skald.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

An s-class skald is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, light and medium armor, and shields (except tower shields). An s-class skald can cast skald spells while wearing light or medium armor and even using a shield without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance.

This does not affect the arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes. Like other arcane spellcasters, an s-class skald wearing heavy armor incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has somatic components.

Bardic Knowledge (Ex)

An s-class skald adds 1/2 her class level (minimum 1) on all Knowledge skill checks, and may make all Knowledge skill checks untrained.

Skald Clan

Every s-class skald is part of a clan with specific training practices and means of surival. At 1st level, choose an s-class skald’s clan. Once chosen, this cannot be changed. Clans grant benefits at different levels, as detailed in each, and may change the skald’s spellcasting ability modifier.

The clans available at the end of this section are the blood, grove, hex, traditions, and wolf.

Spellcasting

An s-class skald casts arcane spells drawn from the bard spell list. She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time.

Every skald spell has a verbal component—these verbal components can take the form of song, recitation, or even non-verbal music like percussion. To learn or cast a spell, an s-class skald must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell’s level. The saving throw DC against an s-class skald’s spell is 10 + the spell’s level + the skald’s Charisma modifier.

Like other spellcasters, an s-class skald can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Skald. In addition, she receives bonus spells per day if she has a high Charisma score.

The skald’s selection of spells is limited. An s-class skald begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of the skald’s choice. At each new skald level, she gains one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: Skald Spells Known. Unlike spells per day, the number of spells an s-class skald knows isn’t affected by her Charisma score; 2 the numbers on Table: Skald Spells Known are fixed.

At 5th level and every 3 levels thereafter, an s-class skald can choose to learn a new spell in place of one she already knows. In effect, the skald loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least 1 level lower than the highest-level skald spell the skald can cast. An s-class skald may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that she gains new spells known for the level.

An s-class skald need not prepare her spells in advance. She can cast any spell she knows at any time, assuming she has not yet used up her allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level.

Cantrips: S-class skalds learn a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, as noted on Table: Skald Spells Known. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume any slots and may be used again.

Raging Song (Su)

An s-class skald is trained to use music, oration, and similar performances to inspire her allies to feats of strength and ferocity. At 1st level, an s-class skald can use this ability for a number of rounds per day equal to 3 + her Charisma modifier. For each level thereafter, she can use raging song for 2 additional rounds per day.

Starting a raging song is a standard action, but it can be maintained each round as a free action. A raging song cannot be disrupted, but it ends immediately if the skald is killed, paralyzed, stunned, knocked unconscious, or otherwise prevented from taking a free action each round to maintain it. A raging song counts as the bard’s bardic performance special ability for any effect that affects bardic performances.

An s-class skald may learn bard masterpieces.

A raging song has audible components, but not visual components. Affected allies must be able to hear the skald for the song to have any effect. A deaf skald has a 20% chance to fail when attempting to use a raging song. If she fails this check, the attempt still counts against her daily limit. Deaf creatures are immune to raging songs.

If a raging song affects allies, when the skald begins a raging song and at the start of each ally’s turn in which they can hear the raging song, the skald’s allies must decide whether to accept or refuse its effects. This is not an action. Unconscious allies automatically accept the song. If accepted, the raging song’s effects last for that ally’s turn or until the song ends, whichever comes first.

At 7th level, an s-class skald can start a raging song as a move action instead of a standard action. At 13th level, an s-class skald can start a raging song as a swift action instead.

For ease of reference, a full list of the standard raging songs can be found at the end of this section.

Scribe Scroll

At 1st level, an s-class skald gains Scribe Scroll as a bonus feat.

Versatile Performance (Ex)

At 2nd level, an s-class skald can choose one type of Perform skill associated with the skald class. She can use her bonus in that skill in place of her bonus in the associated skills listed below. When substituting in this way, the skald uses her total Perform skill bonus, including class skill bonus, in place of the associated skill’s bonus, whether or not she has ranks in that skill or if it is a class skill. At 7th level, and every 5 levels thereafter, the bard can select an additional type of Perform to substitute.

The types of Perform and their associated skills are: Oratory (Diplomacy, Sense Motive), Percussion (Handle Animal, Intimidate), Sing (Bluff, Sense Motive), String (Bluff, Diplomacy), and Wind (Diplomacy, Handle Animal).

Well-Versed (Ex)

At 2nd level, the skald becomes resistant to sonic effects.

The skald gains a +4 bonus on saving throws made against bardic performance, as well as all sonic or language-dependent effects.

Rage Powers (Ex)

At 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter, an s-class skald learns a rage power that affects the skald and any allies under the influence of her inspired rage. This cannot be a rage power that requires the creature to spend a standard action or rounds of rage to activate it. For example, the skald cannot choose terrifying howl (which requires a standard action to activate), but can choose knockback (which is made in place of a melee attack).

Unless otherwise noted, an s-class skald cannot select an individual rage power more than once.

When starting an inspired rage, the skald chooses which rage powers (if any) to add to the song, and all affected allies gain the benefit of these rage powers, using the skald’s level as their effective barbarian level. The skald uses her skald level as her barbarian level for the purpose of selecting rage powers that require a minimum barbarian level. If the rage power’s effects depend on the skald’s ability modifier (such as lesser spirit totem), affected allies use the skald’s ability modifier instead of their own for the purposes of this effect.

If a rage power requires another rage power (such as disruptive, which requires superstition), the skald cannot grant that rage power to allies unless she can also grant that power’s prerequisite. She may add multiple rage powers to an inspired rage at the same time using this ability (such as granting superstition and disruptive simultaneously).

If a rage power can only be used a certain number of times per day or per rage (such as renewed vigor), each ally affected by the inspired rage song is subject to that limit (with once per rage abilities limited to once per inspired rage).

If the skald has rage powers from another source, she (but not her allies) can use those rage powers during an inspired rage. She cannot select a duplicate rage power, unless that rage power can be taken multiple times.

If the skald has the ability to rage from another source, she can use her skald rage powers during that rage as well.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 4th level, an s-class skald gains the ability to react to danger before her senses would normally allow her to do so. She cannot be caught flat-footed, nor does she lose her Dex bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. She still loses her Dexterity bonus to AC if she is immobilized. An s-class skald with this ability can still lose her Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against her.

If an s-class skald already has uncanny dodge from a different class, she automatically gains improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Spell Kenning (Su)

At 5th level, an s-class skald is learned in the magic of other spellcasters, and can use her own magic to duplicate those classes’ spells. Once per day, an s-class skald can cast any spell on the bard, cleric, or sorcerer/wizard spell list as if it were one of her skald spells known, expending an s-class skald spell slot of the same spell level to cast the desired spell. Casting a spell with spell kenning always has a minimum casting time of 1 full round, regardless of the casting time of the spell.

At 11th level, an s-class skald can use this ability twice per day. At 17th level, she can use this ability three times per day.

Lore Master (Ex)

At 7th level, the skald becomes a master of many different types of lore, and can choose to take 10 on any Knowledge skill check that she has ranks in. Once per day, the skald can take 20 on any Knowledge skill check as a standard action, instead of spending the normal time taking 20 requires. She can use this ability to take 20 on a Knowledge skill check twice per day at 13th level and three times per day 19th level.

Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 8th level and higher, an s-class skald can no longer be flanked. This defense denies enemies the ability to sneak attack the skald by flanking her, unless the attacker has at least four more levels in a class that grants sneak attack than the target has skald levels.

If a character already has uncanny dodge (see above) from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum level required to flank the character.

Damage Reduction (Ex)

At 9th level, an s-class skald gains damage reduction.

Subtract 1 from the damage the skald takes each time she is dealt damage from a weapon or a natural attack. At 14th and 19th levels, this damage reduction increases by 1.

Damage Reduction can reduce damage to 0, but not below 0. Additionally, the skald grants this DR to all allies affected by her inspired rage.

Master Skald (Su)

At 20th level, an s-class skald’s inspired rage no longer gives allies a penalty to AC, nor limits what skills or abilities they can use. Allies with rage class abilities may use features dependent on those abilities without restriction, such as a barbarian’s rage powers and a bloodrager’s blood casting and bloodline abilities. Finally, when making a full attack, affected allies may make an additional attack each round (as if using a haste effect).

Raging Songs
Inspired Rage (Su)

At 1st level, affected allies gain a +2 morale bonus to Strength and Constitution and a +1 morale bonus on Will saving throws, but also take a –1 penalty to AC. While under the effects of inspired rage, allies other than the skald cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skills (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride) or any ability that requires patience or concentration. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the song’s bonuses on Will saves increase by 1; the penalty to AC doesn’t change. At 8th and 16th levels, the song’s bonuses to Strength and Constitution increase by 2. (Unlike the barbarian’s rage ability, those affected are not fatigued after the song ends.)

If an ally has her own rage class ability (such as barbarian’s rage, bloodrager’s bloodrage, or skald’s inspired rage), she may use the Strength, Constitution, and Will saving throw bonuses, as well as AC penalties, based on her own ability and level instead of those from the skald (still suffering no fatigue afterward). However, inspired rage does not allow the ally to activate abilities dependent on other rage class abilities, such as rage powers, blood casting, or bloodrager bloodlines; the ally must activate her own rage class ability in order to use these features.

Song of Marching (Su)

At 3rd level, an s-class skald can use raging song to inspire her allies to move faster without suffering from fatigue. By expending 1 round of raging song, the skald invigorates allies within 60 feet, who may hustle for the next hour; this movement counts as a walk (not a hustle) for the purpose of accruing nonlethal damage and fatigue. The skald must continue to perform the song for the remainder of the hour, otherwise its effects end, but only 1 round of raging song is expended for that hour.

Song of Strength (Su)

At 6th level, an s-class skald can use raging song to inspire her allies to superhuman feats of strength. Once each round while the skald uses this performance, allies within 60 feet who can hear the skald may add 1/2 the skald’s level to a Strength check or Strength-based skill check.

Dirge of Doom (Su)

At 10th level, an s-class skald can create a sense of growing dread in her enemies, causing them to become shaken. This only affects enemies that are within 30 feet and able to hear the skald’s performance. The effect persists for as long as the enemy is within 30 feet and the skald continues her performance. This cannot cause a creature to become frightened or panicked, even if the targets are already shaken from another effect. This is a sonic mindaffecting fear effect, and relies on audible components.

Song of the Fallen (Su)

At 14th level, an s-class skald can temporarily revive dead allies to continue fighting, with the same limitations as raise dead. The skald selects a dead ally within 60 feet and expends 1 round of raging song to bring that ally back to life. The revived ally is alive but staggered. Each round, the skald may expend another 1 round of raging song to keep that ally alive for another round. The ally automatically dies if the skald ends this performance or is interrupted. The skald may revive multiple allies with this ability (either at the same time or over successive rounds) but must expend 1 round of raging song per revived ally per round to maintain the effect.

Skald Clans

A skald represents their clan in and out of battle, bringing honor or shame with their decisions and the actions they take. Skald clans each progress at their own pace.

Standard Skalds and Clans

When a standard skald selects a clan, they replace rage powers, versatile performance, well-versed, and lore master, and their Damage Reduction becomes DR /magic.

Because it’s a direct addition to them, the traditions clan cannot be selected by standard skalds.

Blood Clan

Blood clan skalds use the power of their bloodline to imbue themselves and their allies with greater power.

Spellcasting

A blood clan skald can select spells from the bloodrager spell list as skald spells.

Bloodline

Each blood clan skald has a source of magic somewhere in her heritage that acts as the inspiration for her rage.

Sometimes this source reflects a distant blood relationship to a powerful being, or is due to an extreme event involving such a creature somewhere in her family’s past. Regardless of the source, this influence manifests in a number of ways.

A blood clan skald must pick one bloodrager bloodline upon choosing this clan at 1st level. Once made, this choice cannot be changed.

The blood clan skald gains bloodline powers at 1st level, 4th level, and every 4 levels thereafter. The bloodline powers a blood clan skald gains are described in her chosen bloodline. For all spell-like bloodline powers, treat the character’s blood clan skald level as the caster level.

If the blood clan skald takes levels in another class that grants a bloodline, the bloodlines must be the same type, even if that means that the bloodline of one of the classes must change. Subject to GM discretion, the blood clan skald can change her former bloodline to make them conform.

Destined bloodline powers are summarized here for easy reference.

Destined Strike (Su)

At 1st level, as a free action up to three times per day you can grant yourself an insight bonus equal to 1/2 your skald level (minimum 1) on one melee attack. At 12th level, you can use this ability up to five times per day.

Fated Skald (Su)

At 4th level, you gain a +1 luck bonus to AC and on saving throws. At 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter, this bonus increases by 1 (to a maximum of +5 at 20th level).

Certain Strike (Su)

At 8th level, you may reroll an attack roll once during a raging song. You must decide to use this ability after the die is rolled, but before the GM reveals the results. You must take the second result, even if it’s worse.

Defy Death (Su)

At 12th level, once per day when an attack or spell that deals damage would result in your death, you can attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save. If you succeed, you are instead reduced to 1 hit point; if you succeed and already have less than 1 hit point, you instead take no damage.

Unstoppable (Su)

At 16th level, any critical threats you score are automatically confirmed. Any critical threats made against you confirm only if the second roll results in a natural 20 (or is automatically confirmed).

Victory or Death (Su)

At 20th level, you are immune to paralysis and petrification, as well as to the stunned, dazed, and staggered conditions. You have these benefits constantly, even while not using raging song.

Inspiring Bloodline (Su)

Starting at 2nd level, when she begins an inspiring rage, a blood clan skald also grants her bloodline power to the affected creatures. She grants the next bloodline powers she gains to those creatures at 5th level, and every 4 levels thereafter, up to her 16th-level bloodline power at 17th level.

Grove Clan

Grove clan skalds harness nature for power, turning it into inspirational gifts they can bestow upon their allies as they grow closer to it.

Spellcasting

A grove clan skald uses Wisdom instead of Charisma for spellcasting, and she draws her spells from the druid spell list. Instead of spells known, the skald can prepare any druid spell to which she has access in her skald spell slots.

Spontaneous Casting (Sp)

A grove clan skald can channel stored spell energy into summoning spells that she hasn’t prepared ahead of time. She can “lose” a prepared spell in order to cast any summon nature’s ally spell of the same level or lower.

Nature Sense (Ex)

A grove clan skald gains a +2 bonus on Knowledge (nature) and Survival checks.

Woodland Stride (Ex)

Starting at 3rd level, a grove clan skald may move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at her normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect her.

Natural Influence (Ex)

At 5th level, a grove clan skald gains basic druidic training that allows her to perform better in a natural setting.

Resist Nature’s Lure: The skald gains a +4 bonus on saving throws against the spell-like and supernatural abilities of fey. This bonus also applies to spells and effects that target plants, such as blight, entangle, spike growth, and warp wood.

Trackless Step: The skald no longer leaves a trail in natural surroundings and cannot be tracked. She may choose to leave a trail if so desired.

Wild Empathy: The skald learns to use wild empathy.

She can roll 1d20 and add her skald level and her Charisma modifier to determine the wild empathy check result when altering the attitude of an animal or magical beast (at a –4 penalty).

Venom Immunity (Ex)

At 9th level, a grove clan skald gains immunity to all poisons.

Timeless Body (Ex)

After attaining 15th level, a grove clan skald no longer takes ability score penalties for aging and cannot be magically aged. Any penalties she may have already incurred, however, remain in place. Bonuses still accrue, and the skald still dies of old age when her time is up.

Hex Clan

Hex clan skalds turn to their supernatural patrons for power that they channel through their familiars and turn against enemies.

Spellcasting

A hex clan skald can select spells from the witch spell list as skald spells. Instead of spells known, the skald can prepare any spell her familiar knows (see below) as a witch of her skald level in her skald spell slots.

Familiar: Every hex clan skald has a witch’s familiar from which they draw their spells. The skald’s familiar begins play storing all of the 0-level witch spells plus three 1st level spells of the skald’s choice. The skald also selects a number of additional 1st-level spells equal to her Charisma modifier to store in her familiar. At each new witch level, she adds two new spells of any spell level or levels that she can cast (based on her new skald level) to her familiar. Like a witch, the skald can also add additional spells to her familiar through a special ritual.

Patron Spells: When the skald gains her familiar, she must also select a witch’s patron. At 2nd level, and every three levels thereafter (5th, 8th, and so on), the skald’s familiar learns a new spell from her patron. The spells gained depend upon the patron chosen. As an example, the ancestors patron grants the following spells.

2nd—bless, 5th—aid, 8th—prayer, 11th—blessing of fervor, 14th—commune, 17th—greater heroism

Hex

At 5th level, a hex clan skald gains one hex of her choice.

She gains additional hexes at 11th and 17th level. She cannot select an individual hex more than once. Unless otherwise noted, using a hex is a standard action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity. The save to resist a hex is below, followed by some example hexes for easy reference. 10 + 1/2 the skald’s level + her Charisma modifier

Cackle (Su)

As a move action, the skald increases the duration of each of the following hexes by 1 round if the targets are within 30 feet of her. charm, evil eye, fortune, or misfortune

Charm (Su)

The skald improves the attitude of an animal or humanoid within 30 feet of her by 1 step (hostile, unfriendly, indifferent, friendly, helpful) for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier (Will negates). Whether or not the save is successful, a creature cannot be the target of this hex again for 1 day. This is a mind-affecting charm effect.

At 8th level, this effect improves the target’s attitude by 2 steps.

Evil Eye (Su)

One creature within 30 feet of the skald suffers a –2 penalty on one of the following: AC, ability checks, attack rolls, saving throws, or skill checks for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the skald’s Charisma modifier (Will reduces to 1 round). This is a mind-affecting effect.

At 8th level, the penalty increases to –4.

Fortune (Su)

Once per round for one round, one creature within 30 feet of the skald can roll an ability check, attack roll, saving throw, or skill check twice, taking the better result. That creature must decide to use this ability before the first roll is made. Once a creature has benefited from the fortune hex, it cannot benefit from it again for 24 hours.

At 8th level and 16th level, the duration of this hex is extended by 1 round.

Misfortune (Su)

For one round, one creature within 30 feet of the skald rolls all ability checks, attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks twice, taking the worse result (Will negates). Whether or not the save is successful, a creature cannot be the target of this hex again for 1 day.

At 8th and 16th Level, the duration of this hex is extended by 1 round.

Major Hex

Starting at 17th level, the skald can choose a major hex in place of another hex.

Agony (Su)

One creature within 60 feet of the skald is nauseated for a number of rounds equal to the skald’s level.

A Fortitude save negates this effect. If the saving throw is failed, the target can attempt a new save each round to end the effect. Whether or not the save is successful, a creature cannot be the target of this hex again for 1 day.

Prophecy (Su)

The skald can cast divination once per day. She can spend a full hour casting the spell in place of providing the usual material components.

Traditions Clan

Traditions clan skalds hold closest to that which makes one a true skald; acting as warrior poets, musicians, and storytellers for their people.

Rage Powers (Ex)

A traditions clan skald gains rage powers at 3rd level and every odd level thereafter.

Spell Kenning (Su)

Traditions clan skalds gain spell kenning once per day at 5th level, plus one additional time per day at 8th, 11th, 14th, and 17th level. She also gains one additional 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th spell slot at each of those levels.

Damage Reduction (Ex)

A traditions clan skald gains Damage Reduction at 7th, 10th, 13th, 16th, and 19th level, up to DR 5/–. She only grants up to DR 3/– to her allies during inspired rage.

Wolf Clan

Wolf clan skalds are deadly hunters who stalk prey alongside their companions before striking.

Spellcasting

A wolf clan skald uses Wisdom instead of Charisma for spellcasting.

Hunter’s Instinct (Su)

When a skald selects this clan, she gains the lesser fury companion rage power detailed in the next section. At 5th level, she gains fury companion, and at 9th level, she gains greater fury companion.

Defensive Instinct (Ex)

At 2nd level, when unarmored, not using a shield, unencumbered, and conscious, a wolf clan skald adds her Wisdom bonus (if any) to her AC and CMD. If she is wearing armor or using a shield, she instead adds half her Wisdom bonus to her AC (minimum 0). In addition, the skald gains a +1 bonus to her AC and CMD at 4th level. This bonus increases by 1 for every 4 skald levels thereafter (up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level).

These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks and when the skald is flat-footed. She loses these bonuses when she is immobilized or helpless. These bonuses do not stack with the monk AC bonus class feature.

Heightened Senses (Ex)

At 7th level, a wolf clan skald gains the low-light vision rage power. If she has low-light vision already, she gains the night vision rage power instead. If she has darkvision already, she gains the primal scent rage power instead.

Raging Athlete (Ex)

At 11th level, and again at 15th and 19th level, a wolf clan skald can select one of the following rage powers: Raging climber, raging leaper, or raging swimmer. If she already has one of those powers, she can select the associated bestial rage power (such as bestial climber) that comes after it instead.

Rage Powers
Body Bludgeon (Ex)

If she pins an opponent that is smaller than her, she can then use that opponent as a two-handed improvised weapon that deals 1d8 points of bludgeoning damage, assuming the opponent is Small. Larger or smaller creatures used as a bludgeon deal damage based on their size using this base damage. A Tiny creature deals 1d6 points of damage, a Medium creature deals 1d10 points of damage, and so on.

The barbarian can make a single attack using the pinned opponent as part of the action she uses to maintain the grapple, using her highest attack bonus. Whenever she hits using the pinned opponent as a weapon, she deals damage to her target normally, and the grappled opponent used as a bludgeon also takes the same damage she dealt to the target.

If a pinned opponent is unable to resist being pinned for any reason, the barbarian can use that opponent as an improvised weapon without grappling or pinning the opponent, until the creature is reduced to 0 or fewer hit points, at which point the creature becomes useless as an improvised weapon.

Disruptive (Ex)

The DC to cast spells defensively increases by +4 for all enemies that are within your threatened area. This increase to casting spells defensively only applies if you are aware of the enemy’s location and are capable of taking an attack of opportunity. If you can only take one attack of opportunity per round and have already used that attack, this increase does not apply. This counts as the Disruptive feat.

Eater Of Magic (Su)

When she succeeds at a saving throw to resist a spell, supernatural ability, or spell-like ability, she gains temporary hit points equal to the spell’s level (in the case of spells or spell-like abilities) or 1/2 the CR of the effect’s creator (in the case of supernatural abilities). These temporary hit points disappear when the barbarian’s rage ends, and they stack with her temporary hit points from rage but not with other temporary hit points gained from this rage power.

Flesh Wound (Ex)

Once per day, she can avoid serious harm from an attack.

She attempts a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the damage that would be dealt by the attack. If she succeeds, she takes no damage from the attack. If she fails, she takes half damage from the attack and the damage is nonlethal.

The barbarian must elect to use this ability after the attack roll is made, but before the damage is rolled. A barbarian must be at least 10th level to select this rage power.

Fueled By Vengeance (Ex)

Once per round, when she deals damage to a creature that dealt damage to her since the end of her last turn, add 1 round to the barbarian’s remaining number of rounds of rage for the current day.

Fury Companion (Su)

Prerequisites: Lesser fury companion, barbarian level 6th.

A skald with this rage power can instill her fury companion with some of her own rage and anger. When she conjures her companion, the skald can choose to grant it her rage bonuses to attacks, damage, and Will saving throws while she rages and it remains within 50 feet of her. Each round spent in this way counts as two rounds of rage.

Fury Companion, Greater (Su)

Prerequisites: Fury companion, lesser fury companion, skald level 10th.

A skald with this rage power can conjure a stronger fury to aid her against her enemies. When she conjures her fury companion, she can either conjure a druid’s animal companion, or grant her companion her rage bonuses without spending additional rounds of rage (your choice).

Once this choice is made, it cannot be changed (but it can be retrained like any rage power). The skald’s effective level with her druid’s companion is still equal to her skald level –3.

Fury Companion, Lesser (Su)

A skald with this rage power can call on a fury—a vengeful nature spirit—to aid her in combat.

When the skald enters rage, she also conjures a ranger’s animal companion to fight alongside her until it is slain or dismissed, or until her rage ends. This can be a different creature each time. The skald’s effective druid level with her companion is equal to her skald level –3 (minimum 1st).

Even when raging, the skald can concentrate enough to give her companion orders while it remains within 50 feet of her.

The first time she conjures her companion each day, its hit points are full. Each time after, the companion’s hit points are the same as they were when last it disappeared. If the companion was slain, it instead comes back with half its total hit points, and both the companion and the skald suffer a –2 morale penalty on attacks for the duration of rage.

During downtime, the skald can train one of the creatures she is able to call upon without restriction. If she enters combat while attempting to do so, she must enter her rage at the start of her first turn or spend her standard action dismissing her companion.

She gains a bite attack that deals 1d4 piercing damage (if she is Medium) plus her Strength modifier. When used as part of a full-attack action, the bite attack is made at the skald’s full base attack bonus –5, and she adds only 1/2 her Strength modifier to the damage roll.

Guarded Life (Ex)

If she is reduced below 0 hit points, 1 hit point of lethal damage per barbarian level is converted to nonlethal damage. If the barbarian is at negative hit points due to lethal damage, she immediately stabilizes.

Greater: Convert 1 additional hit point per barbarian level.

Intimidating Glare (Ex)

She adds her Strength modifier in place of her Charisma modifier on all Intimidate checks to demoralize a foe.

She can also attempt an Intimidate check to demoralize an adjacent foe as a move action instead of a standard action. If she successfully demoralizes an adjacent foe, that foe is shaken for the remainder of the barbarian’s current rage.

Reckless Stance (Ex)

She can enter a stance which grants her a +1 bonus on attack rolls, but takes a –1 penalty to AC. This bonus and penalty increase by 1 at 4th level and every 4 barbarian levels thereafter.

Regenerative Stance (Ex)

She can enter a stance which grants her 1 temporary hit point for every 4 levels she has (up to 5 hit points per round) at the start of each of her turns, but this cannot give her more than her maximum temporary hit points from rage.

Superstition (Ex)

She gains a +2 morale bonus on saving throws made to resist spells, supernatural abilities, and spell-like abilities.

This bonus increases by +1 for every 4 barbarian levels.

She also cannot be a willing target of any spell and must make saving throws to resist all spells, even those cast by allies. If she chooses superstition with persistent fury, this effect still only occurs while the barbarian is raging.
